Hi Alan —

Quick note: Stripe returned three successive authorization failures for invoice #8237 when attempting to charge the card on file (decline codes in attached CSV). The acquirer is requiring 3DS for this issuer, and the existing token is being blocked at authorization time.

To avoid a chargeback and keep your service uninterrupted, here are practical options we can execute immediately — please confirm which you prefer and any internal approvals needed:

1) Card update: we can send a secure card update link that tokenizes a new card and retries automatically (fastest).
2) Split payment: accept a 50/50 split — we issue an amended invoice and process a partial charge now, then retry the remainder in 7 days (reduces single-auth friction).
3) Wire/ACH: if you prefer bank transfer, we can provide beneficiary + instructions; indicate PO number and we will reissue the invoice with PO reference (this avoids card auth entirely).
4) Temporary hold: we can hold the invoice from dunning for up to 7 days while you resolve with your bank (we rarely do multi-day holds, requires RevOps sign-off).

We also need one quick piece of info for EU tax reconciliation: please confirm your EU VAT ID and the billing address used for the invoice (these two are often the reason acquirers flag cross-border auths).

Attached: decline_report_8237.csv, invoice_8237.pdf, bank_instructions.pdf (wire details).

If you can reply with the PO number + preferred option, I will coordinate the rest and loop in RevOps to approve any temporary hold.

Thanks —
